subject: SLO gating, sampling, and audit evidence for hosted API p50/p95
messages:
From: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@kitehealth.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: ops@kitehealth.com
Date: 2026-10-07T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify p50/p95 measurement windows and audit evidence

Hi Stephanie / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we progress the procurement path I need to confirm how Redwood defines and measures the p50/p95 commitments for the hosted API in contract language. A few specific asks from Ops/Procurement: 

- Exact measurement window(s) used to compute p50 and p95 (are these rolling windows, fixed buckets, UTC day, etc.)
- Whether sampling is used for traces/latency calculation and if so the fraction and selection rules
- Which request classes are excluded (e.g., cold-starts, synthetic probes, admin calls)
- What audit-grade evidence Redwood will provide on a regular cadence (raw samples, aggregated CSVs, traces, dashboards) and retention period
- Exception process (how transient bursts or outages are carved out) and the notification timeline to customers

We want to avoid ambiguous SLA language that slows legal signoff. Can you send a concise proposal we can share with our security and procurement teams?

Goal: get a concrete evidence package and measurement definition to reference in the SLO addendum.

Thanks,
Bryan
Ops Lead, KiteHealth
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Bryan Cole <bryan.cole@kitehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-10-07T13:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify p50/p95 measurement windows and audit evidence

Hi Bryan — thanks for the clear list. Below is a compact proposal you can drop into the SLO addendum. I kept it point-by-point so your legal/ops folks can comment inline.

1) Measurement epoch and windows
- Primary computation: rolling 24-hour epoch calculated at each 5-minute cadence. Each 5-minute interval is a bucket; for any given day the p50/p95 are reported as the quantiles over the union of all valid request latencies in that rolling 24-hour epoch.
- Reporting cadence: daily SLO report (UTC day), plus on-demand export for any rolling-24h period.

2) Sampling and selection rules
- Passive telemetry: we capture latency for 100% of production requests used for routing/serving; however, to reduce export size we compute quantiles on full telemetry internally.
- Trace-level exports (full request body/stack traces) are sampled at 1% by default and gated by a deterministic hash of request id; sample fraction can be raised for onboarding or troubleshooting windows by mutual agreement.

3) Exclusions and validity filters (what we do not count)
- Exclude health-check / synthetic probe traffic from p50/p95 computations (these are monitored separately).
- Exclude backend proxy timeouts that return 5xx prior to Redwood processing and any request that fails authentication (non-application errors).
- Transient node warm-ups: requests within the first 30 seconds of a newly provisioned node are tagged and excluded unless persistent across >72 hours.

4) Evidence and retention
- Daily SLO package (CSV) with per-request latency samples used in the day's quantile computation (anonymized request ids, timestamp, latency_ms, region, model_variant).
- Aggregated time-series (5m buckets) and percentile series (p50/p75/p95/p99) in a queryable dashboard link.
- For audits: we can provide a one-week historical raw-sample export (full sampled traces at configured sample rate) and a 90-day retention for aggregated SLO artifacts.
- All evidence exports will include a checksum and timestamped manifest.

5) Exception / carveout process
- Short transient bursts (<= 6 hours) are treated as operational noise and reflected in metrics; no carveout.
- If we observe an incident that materially skews rolling-24h (e.g., regional outage, DDOS, or cross-region networking incident) and it lasts >6 hours, a customer may request a formal carveout. For carveouts >72 hours we will engage a joint review and agree on whether and how to exclude the window from contractual calculations.
- Notification: Redwood will notify the customer within 60 minutes of identifying any incident that may qualify for carveout; a joint review will be scheduled within 48 hours.

Attachments: I attached a short evidence matrix and a sampling probe script to show what the exported CSV looks like. Let us know if you prefer 180-day aggregated retention instead of 90.

If this matches what KiteHealth needs, we can convert to SLO addendum text and circulate to counsel.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Solutions
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: SLO gating, sampling, and audit evidence for hosted API p50/p95

Stephanie / team — quick engineering note to add to the packet (pasting so ops sees exact language):

- "Measurement bucket" = 5-minute wall-clock bucket aligned to UTC (we avoid sliding-quantile at sub-minute resolution for auditability). Quantiles are computed from the union of valid 5-min buckets over the rolling-24h epoch.
- Sampling determinism: sample selection uses a hash of the request id + customer id to ensure reproducible exports for audits (same requests will be sampled across repeated exports at the same sample fraction).
- Retention: we can extend aggregated artifact retention to 180 days with an elevated data-retention add-on (pricing to be confirmed).
- Implementation note: we exclude requests tagged with internal-probe=true and any response code >=500 at the proxy layer prior to Redwood processing.

I'm attaching a one-page draft SLO paragraph (PDF) we can include in the addendum. Marissa / Lauren — if legal wants narrower carveout windows or different notification SLAs, flag it here and we'll adapt.

[Karthik Iyer]
[Attachment: slo-measurement-draft.pdf (document, 12KB)]
